thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] us-east-1 prefix-kv miss rate spike detected. metric: prefix_kv.miss_rate = 0.62 (baseline ~0.04) | 5xx spike on inference-gateway | paged: @tanja-oncall :rotating_light:

tanja-oncall: oncall ack, I'm looking. grabbing dashboards + logs. any obvious deploys in the last 20m?

emily.sre: I see the same on dashboards -> https://internal.redwood/dashboards/prefix_kv?id=us-east-1 spike starts at 21:02:40 UTC, correlated with increased p99 latency for text-generate routes.

logs-bot: recent relevant deployments:
- prefetch-service: deploy 9a3f2c -> rolled at 21:03:12 UTC (tag: prefetch-v2)
- runtime-config: no changes in last hour

jay.eng-runtime: hmm prefetch-v2 changed key namespace separator from ":" to "::" in one code path. that could increase miss rate if prefixes don't match existing warm keys.

tanja-oncall: can we get a KV access sample for a hot route? share ranges for prefix keys and a few miss logs.

emily.sre: pulling sample logs now, tailing gateway and kv layer. attaching snippets below.

emily.sre: ```
21:02:41 gateway: req_id=abcd123 route=text-generate user=acct-42 latency=310ms status=503
21:02:41 kv: key=prefix:user:acct-42:ctx miss -> forwarding to backend
21:02:42 kv: key=prefix::user::acct-42::ctx miss -> backend cold fetch
21:02:42 backend: fetch ok, populate -> duration=110ms
21:02:43 gateway: req_id=abcd124 route=text-generate user=acct-99 latency=320ms status=200
```

jay.eng-runtime: that snippet is telling: we have two key shapes `prefix:user:...` and `prefix::user::...`. prefetch-v2 introduced the double-colon shape for some code paths. KV lookup performs exact key match so those won't hit. mass invalidation isn't necessary; it's just namespace mismatch causing misses (missstorm).

sam-support: I have three customer tickets opened this minute mentioning timeouts and 503s for generation. acct-42 and acct-77 flagged high error rate. CS is routing urgent to AE.

emily.sre: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback prefetch-v2 to restore old key shape; 2) add a compatibility lookup that checks both key formats (slower) until rewarm completes; 3) increase cache capacity/eviction thresholds to reduce churn.

jay.eng-runtime: agree rollback is fastest to stop customer impact. compatibility shim could be follow-up.

deploy-bot: rollback-request received: revert prefetch-service to tag prefetch-v1 by @tanja-oncall. Confirm with `confirm rollback` command within thread.

tanja-oncall: confirm rollback.

deploy-bot: rollback started -> prefetch-service revert to prefetch-v1 (deploy id: revert-9a3f-2107723502). estimated 2m. notifying infra.

emily.sre: measured metrics during rollback: miss rate trending down: 21:05:10 UTC prefix_kv.miss_rate = 0.33 -> 21:07:00UTC = 0.09. p99 latency improving.

incident-bot: update: incident state -> mitigation in progress (rollback), customer impact: high for 2 accounts, elevated errors, region us-east-1.

jay.eng-runtime: adding timeline draft (EMILY/JAY) ->
- 21:02:40 UTC: spike begins, gateway 5xx rises
- 21:03:12 UTC: prefetch-v2 rollout completed (deploy-bot note)
- 21:03:50 UTC: first customer ticket for acct-42
- 21:04:10 UTC: SRE alerted by monitors, page fired to @tanja-oncall
- 21:05:00 UTC: hypothesis: key namespace mismatch (prefetch-v2)
- 21:06:00 UTC: rollback initiated by @tanja-oncall
- 21:08:20 UTC: miss rate falls close to baseline, errors subside

emily.sre: sharing logs for postmortem: https://logs.redwood/streams/2107723333/missstorm-sample (contains full raw kv/gateway traces)

sam-support: escalations: acct-42, acct-77, acct-101 opened P1 tickets. not yet SLA breach but close. I've notified AE + AM for those accounts.

jay.eng-runtime: root cause hypothesis (high confidence): prefetch-v2 introduced a new key encoding for certain code paths (double-colon separator). rollout caused a fraction of traffic to write/read using new keys, resulting in widespread cold misses because warm keys use single-colon format. combination of miss amplification + normal eviction led to transient missstorm.

emily.sre: evidence: cross-check of key counts pre/post deploy shows new key format short-lived spike in unique key cardinality. eviction logs show backend thrash for same logical prefix.

tanja-oncall: immediate follow-ups before full RCA:
- rollback confirmed and completed (deploy-bot finished revert at 21:07:12 UTC) -> owner: @tanja-oncall (done)
- CS outreach: contact top impacted accounts with incident summary -> owner: @sam-support (in-progress)
- temp compatibility shim: read both key formats for 24h while we rewarm -> owner: @jay.eng-runtime (opt-in)
- add unit/regression test to detect key-encoding mismatches -> owner: @jay.eng-runtime (postmortem)

deploy-bot: revert-9a3f-2107723502 completed successfully across us-east-1 nodes at 21:07:12 UTC.

emily.sre: metrics snapshot after rollback (21:09:00 UTC): prefix_kv.miss_rate=0.045, gateway_5xx_rate back to baseline, p99 latency back within SLO.

sam-support: flagged customers notified. will attach incident follow-up notes and escalation log to each ticket.

jay.eng-runtime: long-term action items:
- add compatibility lookup in runtime (checks both shapes for 48h) -> reduce blast radius for future rollouts
- preflight test for key-format invariant in pre-deploy pipeline
- schedule canary that verifies cache hit-rate and warm keys before broad rollout

emily.sre: for the RCA doc we should include: timeline, deploy diff (what changed), key examples, evict/thrash logs, mitigation steps and customer impact timeline. I'll draft and tag owners.

incident-bot: incident state -> mitigated. recommended: create an incidents/ folder RCA with timeline and link to logs.

tanja-oncall: thanks all for fast triage. I'll close the live incident now and move this to RCA phase.

sam-support: noting CS followups: email sent to acct-42 + acct-77 + acct-101 with summary and next steps.

emily.sre: assigning RCA doc to @emily.sre and @jay.eng-runtime. ETA for draft: EOD today.

jay.eng-runtime: leaving a note: avoid key-format changes without cache compatibility layer or rolling warmup. learned.
